questions.stem: A nurse is suctioning an adult client through an artificial airway. Which technique is consistent with current AARC guidance?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Apply suction continuously while advancing the catheter deeply until resistance is met, because deep suctioning is preferred for routine secretion removal.","B":"Preoxygenate as indicated, use sterile technique for open suctioning, and limit each suction application to no more than about 15 seconds during the procedure.","C":"Instill normal saline routinely before every suction pass because lavage improves secretion clearance and is recommended for all artificial-airway suctioning.","D":"Use scheduled deep suctioning even without clinical indications because routine suctioning prevents secretion retention more effectively than as-needed assessment."}}
questions.rationale: The 2022 AARC guideline recommends preoxygenation for adult and pediatric artificial-airway suctioning, sterile technique for open suctioning, avoidance of routine normal saline instillation, and a maximum suction application of 15 seconds. Deep suctioning is reserved for situations in which shallow suctioning is ineffective. Option B is correct.
questions.source_name: AARC — Clinical Practice Guidelines: Artificial Airway Suctioning (2022)
questions.source_detail: AARC recommends preoxygenation, sterile technique for open suctioning, generally avoiding normal saline, limiting suction application to a maximum of 15 seconds, and using deep suctioning only when shallow suctioning is ineffective.

questions.stem: Which action is appropriate when caring for a client with a chest tube connected to a drainage system?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Place the drainage system on the bed beside the client so the tubing remains level with the chest and gravity does not increase pleural drainage.","B":"Keep the drainage system upright and below the client's chest to promote drainage and reduce the risk of fluid flowing back toward the pleural space.","C":"Raise the drainage system above the chest during repositioning because temporary elevation prevents excessive negative pressure and protects the lung from injury.","D":"Clamp the chest tube routinely during transport because an open drainage pathway increases the risk of pneumothorax whenever wall suction is disconnected."}}
questions.rationale: A chest drainage system should remain upright and below the chest or insertion site to facilitate drainage and prevent fluid from flowing backward toward the pleural space. Routine elevation above the chest or unnecessary clamping can create hazards. Option B is correct.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Care of a Chest Tube
questions.source_detail: Current chest-tube guidance states that the drainage system should be upright and positioned below chest level to facilitate drainage and prevent fluid or air backflow.

questions.stem: Which intervention is most important for maintaining an indwelling urinary catheter drainage system and reducing CAUTI risk?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Disconnect the catheter from the collection tubing once per shift so the tubing can be rinsed and inspected before the closed system is reassembled.","B":"Rest the collection bag on the floor when the client is in bed because this keeps the bag below the bladder and improves dependent drainage.","C":"Maintain a closed drainage system, keep the tubing free of kinks, and keep the collection bag below bladder level without allowing it to touch the floor.","D":"Replace the catheter and drainage bag at fixed daily intervals even when the system remains intact because routine replacement reduces bacterial colonization."}}
questions.rationale: CDC CAUTI guidance recommends maintaining a closed drainage system and unobstructed urine flow, keeping tubing free of kinks, and keeping the collection bag below bladder level without placing it on the floor. Routine fixed-interval replacement is not recommended. Option C is correct.
questions.source_detail: CDC recommends a closed drainage system, unobstructed urine flow, kink-free tubing, and a collection bag below bladder level that does not rest on the floor.

questions.stem: When performing an aseptic wound-care procedure involving sites with different contamination levels, which sequencing principle is appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Move repeatedly from the most contaminated area back to the least contaminated area so the same supplies distribute cleansing solution evenly throughout the wound.","B":"Begin with the most contaminated portion because organisms should be loosened first before cleaner tissue is handled with the same instruments and materials.","C":"Clean all areas in random order because contamination level does not affect aseptic sequencing as long as sterile gloves are worn throughout the procedure.","D":"Work from the least contaminated area toward the more contaminated area, using technique and supplies that prevent carrying organisms back toward cleaner tissue."}}
questions.rationale: General aseptic sequencing follows a clean-to-dirty principle, moving from the least contaminated toward the more contaminated sites while avoiding transfer back to cleaner areas. Wound irrigation should also use enough pressure to cleanse without traumatizing tissue or driving organisms deeper. Option D is correct.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Nursing Skills: Aseptic Technique and Wound Care
questions.source_detail: NCBI Nursing Skills states that aseptic procedures generally proceed from clean to dirty, working from least to most contaminated sites and parts; wound irrigation should cleanse without driving bacteria deeper.

questions.stem: Which statement about human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"HPV vaccination treats established HPV infection and removes existing precancerous lesions, so it is primarily used after abnormal screening results are confirmed.","B":"HPV vaccination prevents new infections with vaccine HPV types and helps prevent multiple HPV-associated cancers as well as most genital warts before exposure.","C":"HPV vaccination is recommended only after sexual activity begins because prior exposure is needed for the vaccine to generate protective immunity against HPV.","D":"HPV vaccination eliminates the need for recommended cervical cancer screening because vaccinated people cannot develop infection from any cancer-associated HPV type."}}
questions.rationale: HPV vaccination prevents new HPV infections and protects against HPV types responsible for most HPV-associated cancers and most genital warts; it does not treat established infection or remove existing lesions. It works best before exposure. Option B is correct.
questions.source_name: CDC — Preventing HPV-Associated Cancers / HPV Vaccine Recommendations
questions.source_detail: CDC states that HPV vaccination prevents new HPV infections, protects against HPV types causing most HPV-associated cancers and most genital warts, and works best before exposure.

questions.stem: An asymptomatic 45-year-old adult is at average risk for colorectal cancer and has never been screened. What does the USPSTF recommend?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Defer screening until age 60 because colorectal cancer screening before that age has no demonstrated net benefit for average-risk asymptomatic adults.","B":"Screen only if gastrointestinal symptoms develop because screening recommendations do not apply to adults who have no signs or symptoms of colorectal cancer.","C":"Begin colorectal cancer screening now; the USPSTF recommends screening average-risk adults starting at age 45 through age 75 using an appropriate strategy.","D":"Perform colonoscopy every year because annual colonoscopy is the preferred USPSTF screening schedule for all average-risk adults beginning at age 45."}}
questions.rationale: The USPSTF recommends colorectal cancer screening for average-risk asymptomatic adults beginning at age 45. Multiple acceptable strategies exist; annual colonoscopy is not the recommended schedule. Option C is correct.

questions.stem: A woman of reproductive age screens positive for intimate partner violence and is not in immediate danger. Which follow-up is most consistent with the 2025 USPSTF evidence?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Provide only a telephone number and end the encounter because brief referral information alone is the evidence-based intervention shown to improve IPV outcomes.","B":"Require immediate separation from the partner because clinicians should determine the safest living arrangement regardless of the patient's preferences or circumstances.","C":"Offer or refer her to a multicomponent intervention with ongoing support, address safety and resources privately, and respect her autonomy in shared decision-making.","D":"Avoid further discussion unless physical injuries are visible because screening-positive patients without acute injury do not benefit from support or referral services."}}
questions.rationale: The 2025 USPSTF recommendation finds benefit when women of reproductive age who screen positive for IPV are provided or referred to evidence-based multicomponent interventions with ongoing support. A single brief referral alone is not equivalent to the supported intervention. Safety assessment should be private and care should respect patient autonomy. Option C is correct.
questions.source_name: USPSTF — Intimate Partner Violence and Caregiver Abuse: Screening (2025)
questions.source_detail: USPSTF recommends IPV screening for women of reproductive age and providing or referring those who screen positive to multicomponent interventions with ongoing support.

questions.stem: An adult's spouse died 14 months ago. The client has persistent intense longing, preoccupation with the death, and major impairment in daily functioning. Which condition should be evaluated?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Normal uncomplicated grief only, because grief-related impairment cannot represent a diagnosable condition regardless of duration, severity, or effect on functioning.","B":"Prolonged grief disorder, while assessing the full DSM-5-TR criteria and considering cultural context, other psychiatric conditions, and functional impairment.","C":"Acute stress disorder, because symptoms more than a year after bereavement are classified as an acute trauma response rather than a grief disorder.","D":"A manic episode, because persistent yearning and preoccupation after bereavement are characteristic signs of elevated mood and increased goal-directed activity."}}
questions.rationale: For adults, prolonged grief disorder requires that the death occurred at least 12 months earlier and involves persistent intense grief symptoms with clinically significant distress or functional impairment; the full DSM-5-TR criteria and cultural context must still be assessed. Option B is the appropriate condition to evaluate, not an automatic diagnosis based on duration alone.
questions.source_name: American Psychiatric Association — Prolonged Grief Disorder
questions.source_detail: APA describes prolonged grief disorder as intense, persistent grief associated with functional impairment and notes that for adults the death must have occurred at least one year earlier before the diagnosis can be made.

questions.stem: Which nursing action best illustrates therapeutic use of self in a mental health setting?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Share extensive personal experiences whenever the client is distressed so the conversation focuses on the nurse's history and creates a friendship outside clinical boundaries.","B":"Remain emotionally detached and avoid self-awareness because the nurse's personality, reactions, and relational style should never influence therapeutic interactions.","C":"Use self-awareness, presence, communication, empathy, and professional boundaries intentionally to build trust and support the client's therapeutic goals and recovery.","D":"Adopt the client's beliefs without reflection because agreement is necessary for rapport and is more important than maintaining professional judgment or boundaries."}}
questions.rationale: Therapeutic use of self is intentional, reflective, ethically bounded use of the nurse's professional self to foster trust and therapeutic outcomes. It depends on self-awareness, relational presence, communication, empathy, and professional boundaries rather than unfiltered self-disclosure or detachment. Option C is correct.
questions.source_name: NIH/PubMed — The Therapeutic Use of Self by Mental Health Nurses: An Evolving Practice (2026)
questions.source_detail: Current mental-health nursing literature describes therapeutic use of self as intentional and reflective use of the professional self to foster connection, presence, trust, and therapeutic outcomes while maintaining ethical boundaries.

questions.stem: A client presents in an emotional crisis but has no immediate medical instability. What should the nurse prioritize early in crisis intervention?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Avoid asking about safety because direct assessment of suicidal or violent thoughts can worsen distress and should wait until the crisis has completely resolved.","B":"Assess immediate safety and urgent needs, listen to understand the crisis, identify supports and coping resources, and connect the client with appropriate assistance.","C":"Focus first on a detailed lifelong psychiatric history before evaluating immediate safety because crisis intervention is ineffective without a complete diagnostic formulation.","D":"Make all decisions for the client and minimize participation because people in crisis cannot contribute meaningfully to safety planning, coping, or resource selection."}}
questions.rationale: Early crisis intervention prioritizes immediate safety and urgent needs, active listening and understanding of the crisis, support, coping resources, and connection to appropriate services. SAMHSA's 988 model explicitly begins with safety assessment, listening, support, and resource connection. Option B is correct.
questions.source_detail: SAMHSA describes crisis counselors as first asking about safety, listening to understand how the problem is affecting the person, providing judgment-free support, and sharing helpful resources.
